subject: ServiceBound: No‑Learning Evidence Flow & Cross‑Border Transfer Controls
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@servicebound.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <procurement@servicebound.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: operational evidence for 'no adaptive training' + subprocessor list

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Legal at ServiceBound needs a concise operational package we can share with our privacy and procurement teams to satisfy two asks in our DPA addendum: (1) a concrete evidence flow showing how Redwood prevents customer data from being used for model improvement (no adaptive training / no‑learn), and (2) an up‑to‑date subprocessor list and a brief description of what each subprocessor does.

Concrete asks:  
- One‑page summary describing how runtime capture, prefix caching, and long‑term KV stores are handled (where data is transient vs persisted).
- A short ops runbook (1–2 pages) showing the verification steps you take when a customer opts out of training.
- Subprocessor CSV with company name, role, and country of processing.
- Any recent audit or SOC2 section references that cover the controls.

Do you have those artifacts available? We need them by EOD next Tuesday (2/28) for our internal review. If anything requires escalation, loop in your security or ops contacts.

Best,
Alex
Alex Mercer
Sr. Contracts Manager | ServiceBound Inc.
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@servicebound.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <procurement@servicebound.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 12:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational evidence for 'no adaptive training' + subprocessor list

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We can get a scoped package together by your 2/28 deadline. High level plan:  

1) One‑page executive summary (controls + guardrails) — Kim to own (attached).
2) Ops runbook for opt‑out (verification and enforcement steps) — Soojin to author; will include playbook snippets for toggling learning flags, KV retention, and evidence capture.
3) Subprocessor inventory — Marissa to provide CSV export (company, role, country, contract status).
4) Relevant SOC2/control pointers and internal audit references — David to include section citations and date of most recent review.

We will attach the artifacts into an evidence pack and provide a short recording (if useful) that walks through the runbook. Quick Qs:  
- Are you asking for a formal attestation (signed) or operational artifacts only?
- Any specific geographic residency constraints we should call out explicitly (EU vs US)?

I'll circulate drafts by Thursday EOD (2/24) for internal review. If you'd like an interim call, happy to set one up.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Privacy Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@servicebound.com>, Priya Shah <procurement@servicebound.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 10:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational evidence for 'no adaptive training' + subprocessor list

Kimberly / team — draft ops runbook attached as PDF stub (ops_runbook_no_learn.pdf). Pulling key excerpts here for Alex so ServiceBound can see the mechanics:  

- Toggle architecture: customer flag at control plane -> policy propagated to serving runtime -> runtime disables persistent KV writes and routes traffic through ephemeral cache only.  
- Verification: ops script 'verify_no_learn.sh' checks config hashes and recent write logs; automated proof bundle generated (config snapshot + last 72h traffic sample) when opt‑out is enabled.
- Subprocessor interactions: when opt‑out is active, downstream archival exports to analytics partners are suppressed via policy header 'X-No-Learn: true' enforced at ingestion gateway.
- Evidence artifacts: config snapshot (.json), recent write log snippets (.log), signed internal attestation (.pdf).

Attachments included in final pack: ops_runbook_no_learn.pdf (full runbook), kms_residency_diagram.png (high level), and a CSV of current subprocessors (subprocessors_v2.csv).

Note: for cross‑border residency controls, we use KMS key lineage and region tags on storage buckets; David will enumerate the sections in our SOC2 that map to those controls.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Infrastructure Security | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@servicebound.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <procurement@servicebound.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational evidence for 'no adaptive training' + subprocessor list

Kimberly / team — thanks, this looks promising. A few clarifications before our internal review:  

- Attestation: ServiceBound legal will likely request a signed attestation that the opt‑out process prevents data from being used for any model training or parameter updates at Redwood and any subprocessors it engages for inference telemetry. We don't need formal certification immediately, but a signed statement referencing the runbook/process would be required for procurement to move forward.
- CSV detail: could you add a column indicating whether each subprocessor has access to raw request/response payloads or only aggregated telemetry?
- Timeline: we still need the final pack by EOD 2/28. If a signature is required we can receive it as a PDF via DocuSign link; otherwise an email attestation is fine for now.

If you prefer, we can escalate to procurement leads and signers on our side — Priya is on copy.

Regards,
Alex
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@servicebound.com>, Priya Shah <procurement@servicebound.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Feb 2027 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational evidence for 'no adaptive training' + subprocessor list

Alex / Priya — attached is the evidence pack per your checklist. Summary of deliverables enclosed and next steps below. Attachments:  
- subprocessors_v2.csv (columns: company, role, country, access_to_raw_payloads, contract_status)
- ops_runbook_no_learn.pdf (runbook excerpt + verification commands)
- kms_residency_diagram.png (key lineage by region)
- signed_attestation_no_learn.pdf (internal signatory: Kimberly Park, Head of Trust & Privacy Ops)  [attachment stub]  

What this attestation covers (high level): Redwood will not use ServiceBound production request/response payloads to update or fine‑tune any models or otherwise perform adaptive training on customer data. The attestation points to the runbook verification commands and lists the evidence artifacts we can provide on request (config snapshots, write‑log snippets).

Next steps:  
1) If ServiceBound requires DocuSign, please send the envelope link and signers; we'll route to our Legal signatory.
2) If you need additional samples for onshore residency proof (e.g., bucket ACL exports or KMS key logs), David can generate a short extract.
3) We'll keep subprocessors_v2.csv current and post updates to the Drive folder linked below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cServiceBound-Evidence
DocuSign suggestion link (if helpful): https://www.docusign.com/asset/doc/embedded-sample?id=SB-2027-1142

Thanks — we'll be available for a quick sync if your team wants to walk through the artifacts.

Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Privacy Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: subprocessors_v2.csv (CSV), ops_runbook_no_learn.pdf (PDF), kms_residency_diagram.png (PNG), signed_attestation_no_learn.pdf (PDF)
